# Results — Study 753 (Reverse-Repo-Drain)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The liquidity-plumbing claim —
"a **draining** Fed ON RRP facility marks a **risk-on** regime, so be long stocks" — tested
against month-end SPY. The ON RRP balance is public (FRED `RRPONTSYD` / NY Fed operating desk)
but not on yfinance, so we ship a **small, clearly-labelled, hardcoded monthly proxy**
(end-of-month levels, USD billions, quarter-end spikes rounded) and align it to SPY. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance SPY daily adjusted closes (public, no key), resampled month-end — **total-return** |
| Liquidity series | **hardcoded proxy** for FRED `RRPONTSYD` (ON RRP, Treasury securities sold), end-of-month levels in $B |
| Window | 2021-01-31 → 2025-07-31 (**55** month-ends; **4.5** years); as-of **2026-07-13** |
| ON RRP proxy | peak **$2,554B** (2022-12-31) → **$195B** latest — one fill-then-drain episode |
| Drain regime | RRP falling over the trailing **k** months (default k=3); acted on with a **1-month** lag |
| Entry / costs | 1-month execution lag; timing backtest charges 10 bps one-way per switch |

> **Proxy + sample caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The RRP proxy is a rounded
> transcription of the public FRED series, not a re-derivation — but the verdict does **not**
> hinge on its exact marks. It hinges on the fact that the ON RRP facility has **one**
> meaningful history: a 2021 ramp, the ~$2.55T Dec-2022 peak, and a 2023-25 drain. That single
> fill-then-drain episode straddles the 2022 bear *and* the 2023-24 bull, so any "drain =
> risk-on" spread is an **n=1 macro coincidence**. The block-bootstrap null respects the long
> regimes and says how easily one big drain lining up with one big rally arises by chance.

## The signal — next-month SPY return by drain regime (RRP falling over trailing k months)

1-month execution lag; "fill" = RRP rising. `base` is the unconditional monthly mean. Welch
*t* compares the **drain** mean to the **fill** mean; the block *p* is the share of 20,000
block-resampled label sequences whose drain-minus-fill spread **≥** the observed spread.

| k (months) | n drain | n fill | drain mean | fill mean | base | spread | Welch *t* | block *p* | drain win | fill win |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1  | 28 | 25 | +0.71% | +1.73% | +1.22% | **−1.02pp** | **−0.80** | 0.819 | 54% | 76% |
| 2  | 26 | 26 | +1.23% | +1.01% | +1.22% | +0.22pp | +0.17 | 0.445 | 62% | 65% |
| **3** | 27 | 24 | **+0.94%** | **+1.16%** | +1.22% | **−0.22pp** | **−0.17** | 0.566 | 56% | 71% |
| 6  | 28 | 20 | +1.58% | +0.18% | +1.22% | +1.40pp | +0.92 | 0.065 | 68% | 50% |
| 9  | 27 | 18 | +1.70% | −0.19% | +1.22% | +1.89pp | +1.20 | 0.104 | 67% | 50% |
| 12 | 25 | 17 | +1.60% | +0.23% | +1.22% | +1.38pp | +0.83 | 0.101 | 64% | 59% |

Read it carefully. At the natural "trailing quarter" horizon (**k=3**) the draining regime's
mean next-month return (**+0.94%**) is **below** the filling regime's (**+1.16%**) *and* below
the unconditional base rate (**+1.22%**) — the spread points the **wrong way** (Welch
**t = −0.17**). At k=1 the drain regime *badly* underperforms (win-rate **54%** vs **76%**
filling). The sign only turns positive at long look-backs (k≥6), where "draining" essentially
just re-labels *"we are past the Dec-2022 peak,"* and even there the best Welch *t* is **+1.20**
(k=9) — nowhere near the desk's **|t| ≥ 2** bar, with block *p* = 0.10. The straight
correlation of the trailing-3-month RRP change with the next-month SPY return is
**−0.014** — indistinguishable from zero. There is no horizon at which "drain = risk-on"
clears significance.

## Tradability — a drain-timing rule *loses* to buy-and-hold (the decisive number)

Hold SPY when the RRP (known one month earlier) is draining; otherwise go to cash (long/flat)
or short (long/short). 10 bps one-way per switch; SPY is yfinance **total-return** (auto-adjust).

| rule | exposure | switches (turnover) | gross Sharpe | net Sharpe | net ann. return | buy-&-hold Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **long / flat** | 53% | 14 | +0.52 | **+0.49** | +5.6% | **0.78** |
| **long / short** | 53% | 29 | −0.04 | **−0.08** | −1.3% | **0.78** |

The long/flat drain rule earns a **lower Sharpe (0.49) than simply holding (0.78)** — sitting
out the market whenever the RRP is filling costs more than the drain months return, and the
rule ends at **1.24×** versus **1.61×** for buy-and-hold over the same window. Betting *against*
stocks on filling months (long/short) is outright **negative (−0.08)** — a direct fight with
the equity risk premium. There is no version of this that beats buy-and-hold. **MIRAGE.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and a flat signal stays flat

On a deterministic monthly series with a hump-shaped RRP-like balance (fill then drain) and a
SPY-like price, with a **planted** extra drift during draining months:

| planted drain edge | n drain | drain mean | fill mean | Welch *t* | block *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 64 | +0.95% | +0.42% | **0.63** | 0.284 |
| **0.02** (large edge) | 64 | +2.95% | +0.42% | **3.01** | **0.008** |

With **no** planted edge the test stays well below t = 2 (it cannot manufacture significance
from a noise drain). A genuine planted edge drives t to **3.01** and the block *p* to **0.008**
— the inference detects a real drain effect when one exists. The control proves the machinery
is unbiased, so the real-tape Welch *t* that never clears ~1.2 is what an *absent* effect looks
like, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The drain regime does **not** predict higher forward returns. At the
  natural k=1/k=3 horizons the spread is *negative* (drain underperforms fill; Welch t = −0.80 /
  −0.17), the trailing-change-vs-return correlation is ≈ 0 (−0.014), and the only positive
  signs appear at long look-backs where the *best* Welch *t* is +1.20 (block p = 0.10) — the
  desk's **|t| ≥ 2** bar is never met. This is one fill-then-drain episode, not evidence.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A drain-timing rule earns a **lower Sharpe than buy-and-hold**
  (0.49 vs 0.78 long/flat; −0.08 long/short), ending 1.24× vs 1.61×. Being out of an
  up-drifting market whenever the RRP fills costs more than the drain months return. No
  NAV-scale edge.
- **Liquidity tell? — BUSTED.** The RRP drain is a mechanical consequence of QT and the
  post-2023 flood of T-bill issuance draining money-market cash — coincident with one bull
  market, not a leading risk signal. The one episode where a drain "predicted" the rally
  (2023-24) is exactly cancelled by 2021 (a *fill* alongside a bull) and reversed at short
  horizons. "Draining RRP = risk-on" is a story told about a single macro cycle.
